mainTopic: Hanging partitions (מחיצה תלויה): the leniency for water, whether רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי share a view, the ציפורי incident, and רבה's link to רבי חנניא בן עקביא
overview: The גמרא starts with a rule: a beam four טפחים wide across a cistern shared by two courtyards permits drawing water. It first answers that a bucket never drifts more than four טפחים. It then admits that the water still mixes under the beam, and says the real reason is that חכמים were lenient with water. רב supports this: a hanging partition (מחיצה תלויה) works only for water. רבי יוחנן says רבי יהודה in the משנה follows רבי יוסי, who in the סוכה משנה accepts a hanging wall even on dry land. The גמרא rejects that link. רבי יהודה may be lenient only for a rabbinic law, and רבי יוסי may be lenient only for סוכה, not for שבת. The event in ציפורי, where sheets over pillars served as walls to bring a ספר תורה on שבת, followed רבי יוסי's son. The גמרא also clarifies that the sheets were already hanging and were not spread on שבת. Finally, רבה links רבי יהודה with רבי חנניא בן עקביא, whose ruling about a balcony over water continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A four-handbreadth beam permits drawing water
steps.stepSummary: A beam four טפחים wide laid across a shared cistern permits drawing water from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A beam of four handbreadths permits drawing water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: if a beam four טפחים wide lies across a cistern shared by two courtyards, each courtyard may draw water on שבת. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two courtyards did not make an עירוב together, so each side may only use its own water. The beam acts as a kind of divider marking each courtyard's half of the cistern. The question the גמרא now raises is how a beam sitting on top can really separate the water below.

phrases.english: A beam of four handbreadths permits drawing water.
phrases.notes: The beam lies across a cistern that sits between two courtyards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage with a rule about the cistern case from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A beam four טפחים wide over a shared cistern is enough to permit each courtyard to draw water.

steps.title: The bucket might drift to the other side
steps.stepSummary: The bucket could float under the beam into the other courtyard's area and bring up its water.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the bucket goes to the other side and brings up water from there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule. When you lower your bucket, it might drift under the beam into the other courtyard's half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beam is only on top, so nothing physically stops the bucket below. If the bucket drifts over, you would be drawing water that belongs to the other courtyard. That is forbidden without an עירוב.

phrases.english: But the bucket goes
to the other side, and brings up water from there?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא אָזֵיל דְּלִי לְאִידַּךְ גִּיסָא
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a four-טפחים beam permits drawing water.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A beam above the water does not stop the bucket from drifting into the other side's water.

steps.title: A bucket does not drift more than four handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: חכמים know that a bucket never drifts more than four טפחים, so it stays on its own side under a four-טפחים beam.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis have established that a bucket does not move more than four handbreadths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a bucket only drifts up to four טפחים from where it was lowered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beam is four טפחים wide. If you lower the bucket at the beam's edge, it cannot drift past the beam's full width. So it never reaches the other courtyard's area.

keyTerms.meaning: the Rabbis have established (know as a fact)

phrases.english: The Rabbis have established
that a bucket does not travel
more than four handbreadths.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual observation that limits the scope of the concern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bucket could drift anywhere, even into the other side.
steps.terutzMaskana: A bucket drifts at most four טפחים, which matches the width of the beam.

steps.title: The water itself mixes under the beam
steps.stepSummary: Even if the bucket stays put, the water under the beam flows back and forth between the two sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Still, under the beam the water mixes together!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. Forget the bucket: the water itself moves freely under the beam, so you are drawing mixed water from both courtyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer only dealt with the bucket's movement. This challenge is stronger because the problem is the water, not the bucket. A beam on top cannot stop water from flowing beneath it.

phrases.english: Under the beam, in any case,
the water mixes together!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּחַת קוֹרָה מִיהָא הָא עֲרִיבִי מַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer of Step 3 does not fully solve the problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of Step 1, even as defended in Step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Physically, the water flows under the beam, so the two sides' water is never truly separated.

steps.title: The Sages were simply lenient with water
steps.stepSummary: The real reason the beam works is a special leniency of חכמים regarding water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because it is a leniency that the Sages were lenient regarding water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on explaining the beam as a physical barrier. It says instead that חכמים chose to be lenient when it comes to water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying between the courtyards here is only a rabbinic prohibition, so חכמים could relax it. They let a partition hanging above the water count as if it went down and blocked the water. The answer is no longer about physics but about a rabbinic leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: it is a leniency that the Sages allowed for water

phrases.english: Rather, it is because it is a leniency
that the Sages were lenient regarding water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּקַל הוּא שֶׁהֵקֵילּוּ חֲכָמִים בְּמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 4 by changing the reason behind the rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: from physical separation to a rabbinic leniency
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The beam works because it actually separates the water.
steps.terutzMaskana: The beam works only because חכמים were lenient with water.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the beam really separates the water. The גמרא admits the water mixes. The beam works only because of a special rabbinic leniency for water.
steps.whyThisMatters: This leniency explains why a hanging partition (מחיצה תלויה) works for water but not in other places.

steps.title: Does a hanging partition work in a ruin?
steps.stepSummary: רבי טבלא asks רב whether a hanging partition permits carrying in a ruined building.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי טבלא asked רב: does a hanging partition permit carrying in a ruin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a support for its answer. It begins by quoting a question רבי טבלא asked רב, which sets up the support in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruin may still have the tops of its walls hanging in the air, with the bottoms broken away. The question is whether these hanging wall pieces count as if they reach the ground, which would make the ruin a private domain.

keyTerms.meaning: a hanging partition (one that does not reach the ground)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Tavla asked of Rav:
A hanging partition, does it permit carrying in a ruin?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a מחיצה תלויה counts as a real partition on dry land (in a ruin).

steps.title: רב: a hanging partition works only for water
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that a מחיצה תלויה permits only in water, because חכמים were lenient with water.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A hanging partition permits only in water; it is a leniency that the Sages were lenient regarding water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that a hanging partition does not work in a ruin. It works only with water. This proves the גמרא's answer in Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב uses the exact same phrase as Step 5: water gets a special leniency. So the beam over the cistern is a hanging partition that works only because of this water leniency. On dry land it would not help.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, a מחיצה תלויה works only for water, as a rabbinic leniency. It does not work on dry land, such as in a ruin.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין מְחִיצָה תְּלוּיָה מַתֶּרֶת אֶלָּא בְּמַיִם,
phrases.english: He said to him: A hanging partition permits only in water,
it is a leniency that the Sages were lenient regarding water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְחִיצָה תְּלוּיָה מַתֶּרֶת אֶלָּא בְּמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי טבלא's question, and the answer supports Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in Step 5 that the beam works because of a leniency for water.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's answer to רבי טבלא, which uses the same phrase.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No, a מחיצה תלויה does not work in a ruin, only in water.

steps.title: רבי יהודה follows רבי יוסי on hanging partitions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה in the משנה, and רבי יוחנן explains that he follows רבי יוסי, who says a מחיצה תלויה works even on dry land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: a partition is no greater. רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי יהודה said this following רבי יוסי, who said a hanging partition permits even on dry land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה. It quotes רבי יהודה, who says there is no need for a partition inside the cistern. Then רבי יוחנן explains the source of his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה says a partition inside the cistern is no better than the wall above it. In other words, the wall between the courtyards already counts as if it goes down into the water. רבי יוחנן says this matches רבי יוסי, who holds that a hanging partition works everywhere, even on land, so it is not a special water leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: a partition should not be (greater than the wall); start of a quote from the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on a מחיצה תלויה. According to רב, it works only for water, as a leniency. According to רבי יוסי (followed by רבי יהודה), it works even on dry land.
steps.confusionAlert: The quote 'לא תהא מחיצה' is cut short. The full line in the משנה is 'a partition is no greater than the wall between them.' רבי יהודה is not saying 'there should be no partition' as a ban. He means the wall above already does the job.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, לֹא תְּהֵא מְחִיצָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: a partition should not be (greater than the wall between them).
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, shortened.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֲמָרָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said it following the opinion of Rabbi Yosei,
who said: a hanging partition
permits even on dry land.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּשִׁיטַת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֲמָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה. It contrasts with רב's view that a מחיצה תלויה works only in water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה's ruling that no partition is needed in the cistern follows רבי יוסי, who holds that a מחיצה תלויה works even on dry land.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי יהודה's view rests on a broader principle, not on the special water leniency used by the חכמים.

steps.title: The source for רבי יוסי: walls lowered from above in a סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in Sukkah. The תנא קמא says walls hanging more than three טפחים off the ground are invalid. רבי יוסי says ten טפחים of wall is enough even when it hangs from above.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If someone lowers walls from the top downward, and they are three טפחים above the ground, the סוכה is invalid. If he builds them from the bottom upward, then if they are ten טפחים high, the סוכה is valid. רבי יוסי says: Just as from the bottom upward ten is enough, so too from the top downward ten is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for what רבי יוחנן just said. It shows the משנה where רבי יוסי says a wall hanging in the air still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא holds that a gap of three טפחים under a hanging wall ruins it, because animals can pass under it. רבי יוסי says that once there are ten טפחים of wall, we treat it as if it reaches the ground. That is the idea of מחיצה תלויה, and it is the same idea רבי יהודה used for the courtyard wall that passes over the cistern.

keyTerms.meaning: one who lowers or lets down (walls from above)
from above going downward (a hanging wall)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different directions here. Walls built from the ground up only need to be ten טפחים tall, and everyone agrees about that. The argument is only about walls hanging down from the roof that do not reach the ground.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: One who lowers walls from above going downward,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in סוכה, chapter 1, משנה 8.

phrases.english: when they are higher than the ground
by three handbreadths, the sukka is invalid.

phrases.aramaic: מִמַּטָּה לְמַעְלָה, אִם גְּבוֹהוֹת עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים — כְּשֵׁירָה.
phrases.english: From below going upward, if they are ten handbreadths high, it is valid.
phrases.notes: This is valid even if the walls do not reach the roofing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Just as from below going upward, ten handbreadths are enough,
so too from above going downward, ten handbreadths are enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It gives the משנה source for רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי יוסי accepts a מחיצה תלויה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי יוסי holds a hanging partition is valid even on dry land
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה סוכה 1:8, where רבי יוסי says ten טפחים of wall lowered from above is valid

steps.title: The two opinions may not depend on each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבי יוחנן's link. Maybe neither רבי יהודה nor רבי יוסי holds like the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is not so. רבי יהודה does not hold like רבי יוסי, and רבי יוסי does not hold like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea that רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי say the same thing. This is a short headline, and the explanation comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן tied the two opinions together. The גמרא says they could each stand alone. It is about to show a difference in both directions: why רבי יהודה might reject רבי יוסי, and why רבי יוסי might reject רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: but this is not so (a rejection formula)
holds like (agrees with the view of)

phrases.english: But this is not so,

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: neither does Rabbi Yehuda hold like Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: nor does Rabbi Yosei hold like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the link that רבי יוחנן drew in Step 8 and that Step 9 supported.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי יהודה's opinion depends on רבי יוסי's opinion
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two cases differ, so agreeing in one case does not force agreeing in the other.

steps.title: רבי יהודה may only be lenient for a rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's leniency was only for עירובי חצירות, which is דרבנן. For a סוכה, which is דאורייתא, he may not accept a hanging wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה does not hold like רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה only said his ruling about עירובי חצירות, which is דרבנן. But a סוכה, which is דאורייתא, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of its rejection. It shows why רבי יהודה might not agree with רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used a hanging partition over the cistern, and that only matters for carrying between courtyards, which is a rabbinic rule. Rabbis can be lenient with their own rules. For a סוכה, which is a Torah מצוה, רבי יהודה might demand a real wall, so he need not agree with רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: he only said his ruling up to here (that is, only in this case)
joining courtyards so people may carry between them on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common tool in the גמרא: a leniency said about a rabbinic law does not prove the same leniency for a Torah law.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לָא סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda does not hold like Rabbi Yosei:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda stated his opinion only
with regard to joining courtyards, which is a rabbinic law,
but for a sukka, which is a Torah law, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא בְּעֵירוּבֵי חֲצֵירוֹת דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It explains the first half of the rejection in Step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רבי יהודה must agree with רבי יוסי about a סוכה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A rabbinic law (עירובי חצירות) can be treated more leniently than a Torah law (סוכה).

steps.title: רבי יוסי may not hold like רבי יהודה either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes breaking the link. רבי יוסי was lenient about a hanging wall only for סוכה, which is just an איסור עשה. For שבת, which carries סקילה, he may never have said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי does not necessarily agree with רבי יהודה either. רבי יוסי only said his leniency about a סוכה, which is merely a positive-commandment prohibition. But about שבת, which is a prohibition punishable by stoning, he did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the other half of the rejection. Just as רבי יהודה may not agree with רבי יוסי, רבי יוסי may not agree with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 the גמרא said רבי יהודה was lenient only because עירובי חצירות is דרבנן. Now it says רבי יוסי was lenient only because סוכה is a lighter commandment, an עשה with no court punishment. שבת is so severe, carrying סקילה, that רבי יוסי might be strict even about its rabbinic laws, so the two rabbis' leniencies may not overlap at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition that comes from a positive commandment, which is lighter and carries no court punishment
A prohibition punishable by stoning, the most severe level
'He only said this as far as...': it limits a rabbi's ruling to its original case

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבי יוסי definitely forbids hanging walls on שבת. It only says we cannot prove he allows them there, which is enough to break רבי יוחנן's link.
steps.whyThisMatters: Together with step 11, this fully undoes רבי יוחנן's claim from step 8. Each rabbi's leniency may be tied to how light his own case is.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei does not hold like Rabbi Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei only stated his view
regarding a sukkah, which is a positive-commandment prohibition,
phrases.notes: There is no court punishment for failing to keep סוכה.

phrases.english: but regarding Shabbat, which is a prohibition punishable by stoning —
he did not say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided rejection that began in step 10. Step 11 limited רבי יהודה, and this step limits רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the assumption that רבי יוסי's leniency for סוכה carries over to שבת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes a leniency in a light commandment (an עשה) also applies to a very severe area (סקילה)

steps.title: Objection from the incident in ציפורי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא expects a challenge: in ציפורי people relied on a hanging wall on שבת. Wasn't that done based on רבי יוסי?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will ask: that incident which happened in ציפורי, on whose authority was it done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an objection to what it just said. There was a well-known event in ציפורי where a hanging wall was used on שבת, so maybe רבי יוסי does allow it on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי lived in ציפורי, so people would assume a ruling made there came from him. If so, he clearly allowed a hanging wall on dry land on שבת, which would defeat step 12. This step sets up the answer that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you will say': introduces an objection the גמרא expects
A city in the Galil where רבי יוסי lived and taught
On whose authority, meaning whose ruling was followed

phrases.english: And if you will say:
that incident which was done in Tzippori,
phrases.notes: There they relied on hanging partitions on dry land on שבת.

phrases.english: on whose authority was it done?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תֹּאמַר: אוֹתוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה בְּצִיפּוֹרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible objection to step 12's claim that רבי יוסי might not allow hanging walls on שבת
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 12's claim that רבי יוסי did not extend his leniency to שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The incident in ציפורי, רבי יוסי's city, used a hanging wall on שבת, so it seems to show that he allowed it

steps.title: It was done by רבי יוסי's son
steps.stepSummary: The incident followed רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, not רבי יוסי himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was not done on the authority of רבי יוסי, but rather on the authority of רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. The ruling in ציפורי came from רבי יוסי's son, so it proves nothing about רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son, רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, holds that a hanging wall works even on dry land and even on שבת. Because the ruling was his, step 12 still stands: רבי יוסי himself may have limited his leniency to סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Not... but rather': a pattern that corrects a wrong assumption

phrases.english: Not on the authority of Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל פִּי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי נַעֲשָׂה.
phrases.english: but rather it was done on the authority of Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא עַל פִּי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, אֶלָּא עַל פִּי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי נַעֲשָׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection raised in step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ציפורי incident followed רבי יוסי, so he allows hanging walls on שבת
steps.terutzMaskana: The incident followed his son רבי ישמעאל, so רבי יוסי's view on שבת stays unproven

steps.title: רב דימי tells the story of the Torah scroll
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that people once forgot to bring a ספר תורה before שבת. The next day they spread a sheet over pillars and brought it through to read.
steps.simpleTranslation: For when רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: Once they forgot and did not bring a ספר תורה while it was still day. The next day they spread a sheet over the pillars, brought the ספר תורה, and read from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the actual story of the ציפורי incident, as reported by רב דימי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They had no ספר תורה in the shul on שבת. The sheet stretched over pillars made hanging walls along a path, which turned the path into an enclosed area so they could carry the scroll. This depends on accepting a מחיצה תלויה on dry land on שבת, which is רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When רב דימי came' from ארץ ישראל to בבל and reported its teachings
While it was still day, meaning before שבת began

phrases.english: For when Rav Dimi came, he said:
Once they forgot

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הֵבִיאוּ סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
phrases.english: and did not bring a Torah scroll while it was still day.
The next day they spread a sheet over the pillars,
phrases.notes: The sheet hanging down formed walls on both sides of the path.

phrases.english: and brought the Torah scroll and read from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the details of the incident mentioned in steps 13 and 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ציפורי a sheet over pillars served as hanging walls, which let them carry a ספר תורה on שבת

steps.title: How could they spread a sheet on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the word 'spread.' Everyone agrees one may not make even a temporary tent on שבת, so how could they spread a sheet over pillars?
steps.simpleTranslation: They spread it?! Is that permitted from the start? But everyone agrees that one may not make a temporary tent on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב דימי's story. Spreading a sheet over pillars on שבת looks like building a tent, which is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem here is not the hanging walls. It is the act of spreading the sheet on שבת itself, which counts as making a temporary tent. Since everyone agrees this is forbidden, the story cannot mean they did it on שבת as written, and the גמרא will need to explain it differently.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, as a first choice

steps.confusionAlert: Keep two issues apart. Carrying through hanging walls is the topic of the sugya. Making a tent on שבת is a separate prohibition, and it is the only thing this question is about.

phrases.english: They spread it?!
Is that permitted from the start?
But surely everyone agrees
that one may not make a temporary tent on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרְסוּ?! לְכַתְּחִילָּה מִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָא הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רב דימי's story from step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The word פרסו, 'they spread,' in רב דימי's report
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spreading a sheet over pillars on שבת makes an אהל עראי, which everyone agrees is forbidden, so the story cannot be read literally

steps.title: The sheets were already spread, not spread on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords רב דימי's story. They found sheets already hanging on the pillars, used them as walls, brought the ספר תורה, and read from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the story should be told this way: they found sheets already spread over the pillars, and they brought the ספר תורה and read from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 16 by fixing how the story is told. Nobody spread anything on שבת. The sheets were already there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that putting up even a temporary tent on שבת is forbidden. The answer is that the sheets had been hung before שבת. So the people did nothing forbidden. They just relied on sheets that were already hanging as walls for carrying.
steps.confusionAlert: The story still involves sheets used as hanging walls. What changed is only who put them up and when. They were hung before שבת, not on שבת.

phrases.english: Rather: they found sheets spread
phrases.notes: The sheets were already hanging. Nobody spread them on שבת.

phrases.english: over the pillars, and they brought a Torah scroll
phrases.notes: They used the sheets as walls to carry the scroll.

phrases.english: and they read from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מָצְאוּ סְדִינִין פְּרוּסִין עַל הָעַמּוּדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 16 by rewording רב דימי's report.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording of the report: 'spread' becomes 'found already spread'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The people spread the sheets on שבת, which would mean making a temporary tent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sheets were hung before שבת. On שבת the people only used them as hanging walls.

steps.title: רבה: Two תנאים share the same lenient view
steps.stepSummary: רבה says that רבי יהודה and רבי חנניא בן עקביא said the same thing. For רבי יהודה, he points to the view we already discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: רבי יהודה and רבי חנניא בן עקביא said the same thing. רבי יהודה's view is the one we just mentioned.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה makes a new statement linking two תנאים who are both lenient about walls over water. He sets up the next move, which is showing where רבי חנניא בן עקביא says this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's lenient view was discussed earlier: the courtyard wall that passes over a cistern is enough to permit it. רבה claims that רבי חנניא בן עקביא holds the same kind of leniency. To back this up, the גמרא will now quote his ruling.

phrases.english: Rabba said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Chananya ben Akavya
said one thing (the same view).
phrases.notes: Both are lenient about walls over water.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda: that which we said.
phrases.notes: His view, discussed earlier: the courtyard wall over the cistern permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the ספר תורה story to a new link between two תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה and רבי חנניא בן עקביא share a lenient approach to walls over water.

steps.title: The source for רבי חנניא בן עקביא: the balcony over water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the משנה where רבי חנניא בן עקביא rules about a balcony that measures 4 by 4 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The view of רבי חנניא בן עקביא is what we learned in a משנה: רבי חנניא בן עקביא says, a balcony that measures four אמות by four אמות...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבה's claim about רבי חנניא בן עקביא. It starts quoting his ruling about a balcony hanging over water, and the quote continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To show that רבי חנניא בן עקביא is lenient like רבי יהודה, the גמרא cites his words in a משנה. The case is a large balcony, 4 by 4 אמות, built out over water. His actual ruling about drawing water from it comes in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: A balcony (here, one hanging over water)

steps.confusionAlert: The quote stops partway through, so his ruling has not been stated yet. Wait for the next lines before deciding what he permits.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya ben Akavya: as we learned in a Mishnah
phrases.notes: Introduces the source for his view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya ben Akavya says:
a balcony that has in it
phrases.notes: A balcony built out over water.

phrases.english: four cubits by four cubits
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the second half of רבה's claim.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim that רבי חנניא בן עקביא is lenient like רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה with רבי חנניא בן עקביא's ruling about a 4 by 4 אמות balcony over water.
